papers_read.title_as_printed: Association of Qi-stagnation constitution and subjective sleep characteristics with mild cognitive impairment among elderly in community: A cross-sectional study (Liu et al., Eur J Integr Med 2023)

Identifying mild cognitive impairment and its predictors among normal middle adulthood in Pune, Maharashtra: A community-based cross-sectional survey (Gazbare & Palekar, Clin Epidemiol Glob Health 2024)

what_each_reports.P-261: Fuzhou, 1,071 non-depressed adults aged 55-75; MoCA-based MCI prevalence 29.3%. Adjusted OR 2.581 (1.706-3.907) for MCI with joint sleep disturbance (PSQI >= 6) and Qi-stagnation vs neither; sleep disturbance alone OR 1.681 (1.231-2.296); sleep latency OR 1.168 and daytime dysfunction OR 1.261 in the fully adjusted model.
what_each_reports.P-266: Pune, 605 adults aged 40-60; MCI = ACE-III < 88; prevalence 27.77% (95% CI 24.35-31.47). Multivariable risk factors: older age, female sex, lower education, severe perceived stress, low physical activity. Self-reported sleep duration not associated (chi-square p = 0.88; logistic OR 1.44, 0.94-2.19, p = 0.08, row labelled 'Adequate').

quantity_a: Adjusted odds ratio of MoCA-defined MCI for joint PSQI sleep disturbance and Qi-stagnation vs neither, non-depressed Fuzhou adults 55-75.
quantity_b: Point prevalence of ACE-III < 88 'MCI' in Pune adults aged 40-60 (plus multivariable risk factors).
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable for the recorded figures (an odds ratio vs a prevalence). I also checked the one construct both studies measure, sleep: P-261 finds PSQI sleep disturbance and sleep latency associated with MCI (sleep duration significant only univariately, p = 0.025, and dropped from the multivariable model), while P-266 finds self-reported short sleep duration not associated. This is a significant vs non-significant difference on differently defined exposures (PSQI composite vs self-reported <6 h with difficulty sleeping), in different age bands (55-75 vs 40-60) and with different MCI instruments (MoCA vs ACE-III < 88); P-266's OR interval (0.94-2.19) overlaps P-261's sleep-disturbance OR (1.231-2.296). Not incompatible.

gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Fuzhou (China) vs Pune (India) community samples; the record itself sets dataset_equal = No

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: odds ratio vs prevalence; MCI operationalised by MoCA (P-261) vs ACE-III < 88, a clinical rather than research cut-off, in 40-60 year olds (P-266)
independence: Distinct studies, different countries and authors.
grounds: P-261's recorded figure is an adjusted odds ratio for a joint sleep and Qi-stagnation exposure.
P-266's recorded figure is a prevalence of ACE-III-defined MCI in 40-60 year olds.
The two are different metric types in different populations with different MCI instruments, and the record already fails its own dataset gate.
The shared sleep construct differs only in significance, with overlapping intervals and differently defined exposures, which Section 5.2 says is not a data conflict.

evidence_quotes.quote: the risk of suffering from MCI for older adults with sleep disturbance and Qi-stagnation was 2.581 times higher than that for those without sleep disturbance or Qi-stagnation
Prevalence of MCI among adult was 27.77 % with 95 % CI (24.35-31.47).
We have considered ACE-III score of less than 88 as MCI.
Our result showed no association of sleep duration with cognition.

record_defects: gap_magnitude 0.252 is computed between an odds ratio (2.581) and a percentage (27.77%), which is meaningless.
The PDF map titles P-261 as a speech-analysis paper; the PDF text is the Liu et al. Qi-stagnation/sleep study the record means.
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' implies a disagreement bridged by third studies; there is no disagreement to bridge.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Two studies estimating the same sleep-MCI odds ratio with the same exposure definition and comparable MCI criteria, with non-overlapping intervals.
